name: IaaS (Cloud Infrastructure)
description: IaaS includes cloud provider infrastructure logs such as audit activity, VM events, flow logs, storage access logs, Kubernetes control-plane logs, and configuration/inventory changes.
whyItMatters: Cloud infrastructure logs are foundational for detecting unauthorized access, misconfigurations, and lateral movement in cloud environments. Without these, you have no visibility into your cloud control plane.
splunkApps: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services
Splunk Add-on for Google Cloud Platform
technicalAddons: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services

children.name: Containers / Pods / Clusters
children.description: Containers / Pods / Clusters includes Kubernetes and container platform logs such as control-plane activity, audit events, node/runtime logs, and application logs written by containers.
children.whyItMatters: Kubernetes and container control-plane logs reveal cluster admin abuse, risky workloads, and runtime events that complement cloud audit trails.

children.name: Cloud Instances / VMs
children.description: Cloud Instances / VMs includes logs collected from cloud virtual machines through provider agents or VM log forwarding, such as OS events, authentication/security activity, agent health, and optionally application/service logs.
children.whyItMatters: Cloud VM logs extend visibility into guest OS and agent telemetry for workloads that may not yet send logs through a central forwarder.

children.name: Cloud Storage
children.description: Cloud Storage includes logs from cloud object storage and cloud file storage platforms, such as management activity, object/file access requests, lifecycle or replication events, and storage health telemetry.
children.whyItMatters: Object and file storage access logs detect public exposure, ransomware staging, and unauthorized data access in cloud buckets and shares.

name: PaaS (Platform Services)
description: Platform-as-a-Service logs including managed databases, serverless functions, messaging queues, and application hosting platforms.
whyItMatters: PaaS services often contain the richest telemetry for detecting application-layer attacks, data exfiltration via managed services, and privilege escalation through service roles.
splunkApps: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services
technicalAddons: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services

input_fields.label: Number of PaaS applications
input_fields.helper: App Services, Lambda functions, Cloud Functions, etc.

name: SaaS (General)
description: SaaS platform audit and activity logs: admin/configuration changes, authentication and access security, user/object activity, and API/integration events. Sized by tenant count, active users, and integrations — not per-1,000 users.
whyItMatters: SaaS platforms are primary vectors for business email compromise, data exfiltration, and account takeover. Visibility into user activity is critical for detecting insider threats and compromised accounts.
configuredItemLabel: SaaS tenants, active users, and integrations

input_fields.label: Number of SaaS users
input_fields.helper: Licensed or active users across all SaaS platforms

input_fields.label: Number of SaaS platforms
input_fields.helper: Distinct SaaS apps sending logs (M365, Salesforce, etc.)

children.name: Office Productivity (M365/Google)
children.description: Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace audit and activity telemetry: sign-in and admin audit, Exchange/SharePoint/Teams activity, and security/compliance signals routed to Splunk.
children.whyItMatters: Office productivity clouds are the top vector for account takeover and data exfiltration. Centralizing M365/Google audit logs enables BEC detection, DLP correlation, and insider-threat investigations.

children.name: CRM
children.description: CRM platform audit and API activity (Salesforce, Dynamics, HubSpot, ServiceNow CSM, Zendesk): logins, object changes, integrations, and security events.
children.whyItMatters: CRM systems hold customer PII and revenue data. Audit visibility supports fraud detection, privileged access monitoring, and compliance for sales and service operations.

children.name: SSO / Identity Provider
children.configuredItemLabel: # of users enrolled in SSO or MFA
children.description: Identity-provider and SSO/MFA logs (Okta, Entra ID, Ping, Duo): authentication, MFA challenges, admin changes, and federation events.
children.whyItMatters: SSO is the front door to SaaS and VPN. IdP logs are essential for detecting credential theft, MFA fatigue, and unauthorized app assignments.

children.name: Web Conferencing
children.description: Web conferencing audit logs (Zoom, Teams, Webex, Slack huddles): meetings, recordings, admin settings, and sign-in activity forwarded to Splunk.
children.whyItMatters: Conferencing platforms expose meeting content and guest access paths. Audit logs help detect hijacking, data leakage via recordings, and shadow IT conferencing.

children.name: File Sharing / Collaboration
children.configuredItemLabel: # of users in Box, Dropbox, or OneDrive

input_fields.label: # of users in Box, Dropbox, or OneDrive

children.description: Enterprise file-sharing audit logs (Box, Dropbox, OneDrive standalone tenants): file access, sharing links, admin actions, and DLP-related events.
children.whyItMatters: File shares are a common exfiltration path. File-sharing audit trails underpin insider-threat and data-loss investigations.

name: Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM)
description: CSPM tools continuously monitor cloud infrastructure for misconfigurations, compliance violations, and security risks.
whyItMatters: CSPM findings provide critical context for security operations — revealing attack surface, misconfigurations, and drift that could be exploited before an attacker does.
aiOpportunities: Risk scoring based on exposure and exploitability

input_fields.label: Estimated cloud resources
input_fields.helper: Total resources scanned for compliance

name: Cloud Workload Protection Platform (CWPP)
description: Runtime protection for cloud workloads including VMs, containers, and serverless functions.
whyItMatters: CWPP provides runtime visibility into cloud workloads that cloud-native logging cannot — detecting malware, vulnerability exploitation, and anomalous process execution.

input_fields.label: Number of protected workloads
input_fields.helper: VMs, containers, or serverless functions monitored

name: Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB)
description: CASB provides visibility into cloud application usage, enforces data security policies, and detects shadow IT.
whyItMatters: CASB logs reveal shadow IT, unsanctioned data sharing, and policy violations across cloud services — key for insider threat and data loss investigations.

name: Secure Access Service Edge (SASE)
description: SASE converges networking and security functions in the cloud — SD-WAN, CASB, FWaaS, and ZTNA in a unified service.
whyItMatters: SASE logs provide unified visibility into remote user traffic, policy enforcement, and threat detection at the network edge — critical for hybrid/remote workforce security.

input_fields.label: Number of users
input_fields.helper: Remote and hybrid users routing through SASE

name: Windows Servers
description: Windows Event Logs from physical and virtual servers. Select which log channels to collect below.
whyItMatters: Windows Security logs are the backbone of on-premises detection — authentication events, privilege usage, process creation, and policy changes are all captured here.

log_options.name: Security Event Log
log_options.warning_if_disabled: Security Event Log is critical for authentication and endpoint detection use cases.

log_options.name: PowerShell Operational Logs
log_options.warning_if_disabled: PowerShell logs are important for detecting script-based attacks and living-off-the-land techniques.

log_options.name: Sysmon Events
log_options.warning_if_disabled: Sysmon provides deep endpoint visibility for process, network, and file activity.

log_options.name: Performance Metrics
log_options.warning_if_disabled: Performance Metrics are important for IT Ops and infrastructure monitoring use cases.

input_fields.label: Number of Windows servers
input_fields.helper: All Windows servers with event log forwarding enabled

name: Linux / Unix Servers (Production)
description: System logs from production Linux/Unix servers including syslog, auth logs, performance metrics, and security events.
whyItMatters: Linux servers often host critical applications and databases. Auth logs, process execution, and network connections are essential for detecting compromises in *nix environments.
splunkApps: Splunk App for Unix and Linux
technicalAddons: Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux

input_fields.label: Number of Linux servers
input_fields.helper: Production Linux/Unix servers with log collection

name: Linux / Unix Servers (Non-Production)
description: System logs from development, test, and staging Linux/Unix environments.
whyItMatters: Non-production environments are often less secured and can serve as pivot points for attackers. They also contain valuable data for application troubleshooting.
splunkApps: Splunk App for Unix and Linux
technicalAddons: Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux

name: Mainframe
description: Mainframe system logs including SMF records, RACF security events, and system activity.
whyItMatters: Mainframes process the majority of financial transactions globally. Security events from RACF/ACF2/TopSecret are critical for compliance and detecting privileged access abuse.

input_fields.label: Manual estimate (GB/day)
input_fields.helper: Mainframe volumes vary widely — manual estimate recommended

name: Virtual Infrastructure (Hypervisor)
description: Hypervisor and virtual infrastructure management logs from VMware vCenter, ESXi hosts, Hyper-V, and other platforms.
whyItMatters: Hypervisor compromise gives an attacker access to all hosted VMs. Monitoring vMotion, snapshot operations, and admin changes is critical for detecting VM escape and infrastructure manipulation.

input_fields.label: Number of hypervisor hosts
input_fields.helper: ESXi hosts, Hyper-V hosts, etc.

name: Database Instances
description: Database audit logs, transaction logs, access logs, and error logs from relational and NoSQL database systems.
whyItMatters: Databases contain your crown jewels. Audit logs reveal unauthorized queries, privilege escalation, and data exfiltration attempts. Transaction logs support forensic investigation of data breaches.
splunkApps: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft SQL Server
technicalAddons: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft SQL Server

children.name: Transaction Logs
children.description: Database transaction or SQL audit streams capturing DML/DDL activity, sensitive table access, and application database calls.
children.whyItMatters: Transaction-level database telemetry supports fraud detection, data integrity monitoring, and forensic reconstructions after data tampering.

children.name: Access / Audit Logs
children.description: Database access and authentication audit logs (DBA actions, failed logins, privilege use) from enterprise RDBMS platforms.
children.whyItMatters: Database access logs reveal credential abuse, excessive privilege use, and suspicious query patterns that raw transaction logs may not contextualize.

input_fields.label: Number of database instances
input_fields.helper: Individual DB instances (not schemas)

name: Web Servers (Production)
description: Web server access logs, error logs, and performance metrics from HTTP/HTTPS serving infrastructure.
whyItMatters: Web servers are the front door to your applications. Access logs reveal attack patterns (SQLi, XSS, path traversal), while error logs expose application vulnerabilities being probed.
configuredItemLabel: # of production web servers hosting applications
splunkApps: Splunk Add-on for Apache Web Server
technicalAddons: Splunk Add-on for Apache Web Server

input_fields.label: Estimated requests/day (millions)
input_fields.helper: Affects access log volume significantly

name: Web Servers (Non-Production)
description: Web server access logs, error logs, and performance metrics from dev, test, and staging HTTP/HTTPS environments.
whyItMatters: Non-production web tiers are frequently targeted during reconnaissance and often run with weaker hardening. They still generate valuable access and error telemetry for troubleshooting and threat detection.
splunkApps: Splunk Add-on for Apache Web Server
technicalAddons: Splunk Add-on for Apache Web Server

input_fields.label: Estimated requests/day (millions)
input_fields.helper: Lower traffic than production; still affects access log volume

name: Application Servers (Production)
description: Application server logs including J2EE containers, .NET runtime, and middleware platforms.
whyItMatters: Application server logs reveal business logic attacks, session manipulation, and application-layer vulnerabilities that network devices cannot detect.

name: Application Servers (Non-Production)
description: Application server logs from development, test, and staging J2EE, .NET, and middleware runtimes.
whyItMatters: Non-production app tiers often hold production-like data and credentials. Application logs help detect misconfigurations, credential reuse, and lateral movement between lower environments.

name: Middleware Services (Production)
description: Message queuing, ESB, and integration platform logs.
whyItMatters: Middleware is the connective tissue between applications. Monitoring message flows reveals data integrity issues, unauthorized integrations, and service disruption attempts.

input_fields.label: Number of production middleware systems
input_fields.helper: Message queues, ESBs, API gateways

name: Middleware Services (Non-Production)
description: Message queuing, ESB, and integration platform logs from dev, test, and staging environments.
whyItMatters: Non-production middleware often connects to shared services and test data sets. Monitoring message flows reveals integration failures, unauthorized test traffic, and environment bleed-over.

input_fields.label: Number of non-prod middleware systems
input_fields.helper: Dev/test/stage message queues, ESBs, API gateways

name: APM (Application Performance Monitoring)
description: Application performance metrics, traces, and error tracking from APM platforms.
whyItMatters: APM data enriches security investigations with application context — understanding which services were impacted, response time anomalies that indicate compromise, and error patterns from exploitation attempts.
aiOpportunities: Performance anomaly correlation with security events

input_fields.label: Number of instrumented applications
input_fields.helper: Apps with APM agents or OpenTelemetry

name: Public Key Infrastructure (PKI)
description: Certificate lifecycle logs including issuance, revocation, renewal, and enrollment events.
whyItMatters: PKI logs are critical for detecting unauthorized certificate issuance, expired certificates causing outages, and certificate-based attacks like golden certificates in AD CS.

name: SAP
description: SAP application logs including security audit logs, change documents, and transaction logs.
whyItMatters: SAP systems contain highly sensitive business data. Monitoring SAP security logs detects unauthorized access to financial data, payroll manipulation, and fraudulent transactions.

input_fields.label: Number of SAP systems
input_fields.helper: Production SAP instances (ECC, S/4HANA, etc.)

name: Desktops / Workstations
description: Windows Event Logs, macOS unified logs, and Linux desktop logs from end-user workstations.
whyItMatters: Endpoints are the initial compromise point for most attacks. Workstation logs provide process execution, network connection, and authentication data critical for detecting phishing, malware, and lateral movement.
technicalAddons: Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux

input_fields.label: Number of desktops/laptops
input_fields.helper: User endpoints with log collection agents

name: User Authentication (SSO / PAM / IAM)
description: Identity and access management logs from SSO, PAM, and IAM platforms including authentication events, privilege usage, and session management.
whyItMatters: Identity is the new perimeter. SSO/PAM logs are the single most valuable source for detecting credential theft, privilege escalation, and unauthorized access across the entire environment.

input_fields.label: Number of SSO/PAM users
input_fields.helper: Users authenticating through SSO or PAM

name: Active Directory / Domain Controllers
description: Windows Security Event Logs from Domain Controllers capturing all authentication, group policy changes, and directory modifications.
whyItMatters: Active Directory is the identity backbone of most enterprises. DC logs capture every authentication, group membership change, and Kerberos ticket event — essential for detecting Pass-the-Hash, Golden Ticket, and DCSync attacks.
technicalAddons: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Active Directory

input_fields.label: Number of AD users
input_fields.helper: Active user accounts in the directory

name: Email Servers / Email Gateways
description: Email server logs and secure email gateway logs including message tracking, threat detection, and DLP events.
whyItMatters: Email is the #1 attack vector. Gateway and server logs reveal phishing attempts, malicious attachments, BEC patterns, and data exfiltration via email.

name: Mobile Device Management (MDM)
description: MDM platform logs including device compliance, app deployment, and security policy enforcement.
whyItMatters: Mobile devices access corporate data but operate outside traditional network controls. MDM logs reveal jailbroken devices, policy violations, and unauthorized app installations.

name: Vulnerability Management
description: Vulnerability scanner results, compliance scan data, and asset discovery information.
whyItMatters: Vulnerability data provides critical risk context for security operations — correlating active exploits with known vulnerabilities dramatically improves alert prioritization and incident response.

input_fields.label: Number of scanned assets
input_fields.helper: Hosts/IPs scanned for vulnerabilities

name: Network Traffic Analysis / NetFlow
description: Network flow records (NetFlow, sFlow, IPFIX) providing metadata about all network communications without full packet capture.
whyItMatters: NetFlow provides the 'who talked to whom, when, and how much' view of your network. Essential for detecting C2 beacons, lateral movement, data exfiltration, and network reconnaissance.

input_fields.label: Number of flow-exporting devices
input_fields.helper: Routers/switches/firewalls exporting NetFlow/IPFIX

name: Intrusion Prevention/Detection Systems (IPS/IDS)
description: Alert and event logs from network-based intrusion detection and prevention systems.
whyItMatters: IDS/IPS provides signature-based and anomaly-based detection of known attack patterns. While not sufficient alone, these alerts are valuable for correlation with other data sources.

name: Threat Intelligence Feeds
description: Threat intelligence indicators (IOCs), threat actor profiles, and campaign information from commercial and open-source feeds.
whyItMatters: Threat intel transforms reactive detection into proactive hunting. Correlating IOCs against your logs reveals compromises that signature-based tools miss.

name: Automated Malware Analysis (Sandbox)
description: Sandbox detonation results including behavioral analysis, IOC extraction, and verdict information.
whyItMatters: Sandbox results provide ground truth for malware classification and IOC generation. Integrating these feeds enriches alert triage and enables proactive blocking of related indicators.

name: EDR (Endpoint Detection & Response)
description: Endpoint telemetry including process creation, file modifications, registry changes, network connections, and detection alerts.
whyItMatters: EDR provides the deepest endpoint visibility available — process trees, command-line arguments, file modifications, and network connections. This is essential for detecting advanced threats that evade traditional AV.
exampleLog: timestamp=2026-07-06T21:49:45Z host=workstation-042 user=DOMAIN\jsmith vendor_product="CrowdStrike Falcon" event_type=process process_name=powershell.exe parent_process=winword.exe command_line="powershell.exe -enc <encoded_command>" file_hash=SHA256:a1b2c3d4e5 severity=high action=blocked src_ip=10.0.1.42 dest_ip=198.51.100.25

input_fields.label: Number of endpoints with EDR
input_fields.helper: Workstations and servers with EDR agent

input_fields.label: Number of servers included
input_fields.helper: Servers typically generate more EDR telemetry than workstations

name: NDR (Network Detection & Response)
description: Network-based detection and response platform logs including lateral movement alerts, encrypted traffic analysis, and behavioral anomalies.
whyItMatters: NDR provides network-layer behavioral detection that catches threats invisible to endpoint tools — particularly encrypted C2, lateral movement, and data staging prior to exfiltration.

name: Data Loss/Leakage Prevention (DLP)
description: DLP policy violation events, data classification results, and incident alerts from network and endpoint DLP systems.
whyItMatters: DLP logs are essential for detecting and investigating data exfiltration — both malicious insiders and external attackers staging data for theft.

input_fields.label: Number of monitored users
input_fields.helper: Users covered by DLP policies across email, web, endpoint, and cloud channels

input_fields.label: DLP products/channels monitored
input_fields.helper: Count of DLP products or channels (email, web, endpoint, cloud) — planning floor ~0.05 GB/day per channel

input_fields.label: DLP sizing profile
input_fields.helper: User monitoring requires monitored users; channel-only uses product/channel floor rates

name: User Behavior Analytics (UBA/UEBA)
description: User and entity behavior analytics output including risk scores, anomaly detections, and threat indicators.
whyItMatters: UBA/UEBA provides ML-driven detection of insider threats and compromised accounts by establishing behavioral baselines and detecting deviations that rule-based systems miss.

name: Asset & Identity Lists (CMDB / AD / LDAP)
description: Asset inventory, identity directory, and CMDB data used for enrichment and context in security operations.
whyItMatters: Asset and identity context transforms raw alerts into actionable intelligence — knowing the criticality, owner, and classification of impacted assets dramatically improves response prioritization.
configuredItemLabel: # of asset or identity data sources

input_fields.label: Number of asset/identity data sources
input_fields.helper: CMDB exports, LDAP/AD sync sources, or identity list feeds

input_fields.label: Ingest profile
input_fields.helper: Lookup/context sources are enrichment only; periodic/full exports use ~0.025 GB/day per source

name: Deception Technology
description: Honeypot, honeytoken, and deception platform alerts indicating interaction with decoy systems or credentials.
whyItMatters: Deception alerts are extremely high-fidelity — any interaction with a decoy is almost certainly malicious. These provide early warning of lateral movement and credential theft.

name: Firewalls (Next-Gen Firewalls)
description: Firewall traffic logs including allow/deny decisions, URL filtering, threat prevention, application identification, and user-ID mapping.
whyItMatters: Firewalls are the single highest-volume and often highest-value security data source. They provide comprehensive network visibility — who connected where, what was blocked, and which applications traversed the network.
splunkApps: Splunk Add-on for Palo Alto Networks
technicalAddons: Splunk Add-on for Palo Alto Networks
overlapNotes: If using SASE, there may be overlap with cloud-delivered firewall logs. Coordinate to avoid double-counting.

children.name: Perimeter Firewalls
children.description: Internet-facing next-generation firewall traffic, threat, and VPN logs from perimeter appliances and virtual firewalls.
children.whyItMatters: Perimeter firewalls see north-south attacks first. These logs anchor network detection, threat hunting, and compliance evidence for external exposure.

children.name: Internal Segmentation Firewalls
children.description: Internal segmentation firewall logs for east-west traffic between zones, data centers, and sensitive VLANs.
children.whyItMatters: Lateral movement often crosses internal segments. Segmentation firewall logs help validate Zero Trust boundaries and detect east-west C2.

children.name: Web Application Firewall (WAF)
children.description: Web application firewall logs including HTTP/S requests, blocked attacks, bot scores, and OWASP rule hits.
children.whyItMatters: WAF telemetry exposes application-layer attacks before they reach origin servers — critical for protecting customer-facing and API workloads.

input_fields.label: Number of users protected
input_fields.helper: Firewall ingest correlates more with protected user population than device count

input_fields.label: Number of firewall devices
input_fields.helper: Physical/virtual firewall instances — used for confidence scoring

name: Network Switches
description: Switch logs including port security, VLAN changes, spanning tree events, and MAC address table changes.
whyItMatters: Switch logs reveal unauthorized devices connecting to the network, VLAN hopping attempts, and physical security violations at the network access layer.

name: Routers
description: Router logs including routing table changes, BGP events, ACL hits, and interface state changes.
whyItMatters: Routers control traffic flow between network segments. Monitoring routing changes and ACL violations detects network manipulation and unauthorized path changes.

name: VPN Gateways
description: VPN connection logs including user authentication, tunnel establishment, traffic volumes, and disconnection events.
whyItMatters: VPN logs are critical for monitoring remote access — detecting compromised credentials, unusual connection times/locations, and data exfiltration over encrypted tunnels.

input_fields.label: Number of VPN users
input_fields.helper: Concurrent or licensed VPN users

name: Web Proxy / Secure Web Gateway
description: Web proxy logs including URL categorization, content inspection results, and user attribution for web traffic.
whyItMatters: Proxy logs provide URL-level visibility into all web traffic — essential for detecting C2 communications, drive-by downloads, and data exfiltration over HTTP/HTTPS.
technicalAddons: Splunk Add-on for Blue Coat ProxySG

input_fields.label: Number of users
input_fields.helper: Users routing through the proxy

name: Network Access Control (NAC)
description: NAC platform logs including device posture assessment, network admission decisions, and quarantine events.
whyItMatters: NAC logs show which devices were allowed or denied network access and why — critical for detecting rogue devices and ensuring compliance enforcement at the access layer.

name: DNS
description: DNS query and response logs from internal resolvers and authoritative servers.
whyItMatters: DNS is used in nearly every cyberattack — from initial payload delivery to C2 communication to data exfiltration. DNS logs are one of the most underutilized yet valuable data sources for threat detection.

input_fields.label: Number of users generating DNS queries

name: DHCP
description: DHCP lease logs mapping IP addresses to MAC addresses and hostnames over time.
whyItMatters: DHCP logs are essential for attribution — they map ephemeral IP addresses to devices at specific points in time, enabling accurate forensic investigation and alert triage.

name: Load Balancers
description: Load balancer logs including traffic distribution, health checks, SSL termination events, and connection metadata.
whyItMatters: Load balancer logs provide visibility into application delivery and can reveal DDoS patterns, application-layer attacks, and service degradation.

name: DDoS Protection
description: DDoS mitigation platform logs including attack detection, traffic scrubbing, and rate limiting events.
whyItMatters: DDoS logs provide visibility into volumetric attacks, application-layer floods, and the effectiveness of mitigation responses.

name: Wireless Access Points
description: Wireless controller and access point logs including client associations, rogue AP detection, and authentication events.
whyItMatters: Wireless logs reveal rogue access points, unauthorized device connections, and provide location context for security investigations.

name: Deep Packet Inspection / Full PCAP
description: Full packet capture and deep packet inspection data providing complete network transaction visibility.
whyItMatters: DPI/PCAP provides the ultimate network forensic capability — reconstructing exact conversations, extracting files, and validating alerts with packet-level evidence.

name: Production Storage Arrays
description: Storage array logs including access patterns, performance metrics, and administrative changes for production data stores.
whyItMatters: Storage logs detect unauthorized data access, unusual I/O patterns that indicate data staging, and administrative changes that could compromise data availability.

input_fields.label: Number of storage systems
input_fields.helper: SAN, NAS, or object storage arrays

input_fields.label: Manual estimate (GB/day)
input_fields.helper: Storage log volumes vary widely

name: ICS / SCADA Systems
description: Industrial control system logs including SCADA events, PLC state changes, and process variable anomalies.
whyItMatters: OT/ICS systems control physical processes — unauthorized changes can cause safety incidents, environmental damage, or production disruption. Visibility into these systems is critical for detecting targeted attacks.
configuredItemLabel: # of industrial control or SCADA systems

input_fields.label: Number of OT/SCADA systems
input_fields.helper: PLCs, HMIs, RTUs, historians

input_fields.label: Manual estimate (GB/day)
input_fields.helper: OT environments vary significantly

name: OT Security Solutions (OT IDS)
description: OT-specific intrusion detection and asset discovery platform logs.
whyItMatters: OT IDS platforms provide passive network monitoring purpose-built for industrial protocols — detecting threats without impacting sensitive control systems.

input_fields.label: Number of OT security monitoring points

name: CI/CD and Build Systems
description: Build system, deployment pipeline, and CI/CD platform logs including build results, deployments, and artifact management.
whyItMatters: CI/CD pipelines are high-value targets — compromising the build pipeline enables supply chain attacks. Monitoring pipeline activity detects unauthorized deployments, credential theft, and code injection.

name: Configuration Management / Deployment Tools
description: Configuration management platform logs including state changes, compliance drift, and deployment activities.
whyItMatters: Configuration changes are a common attack vector. Monitoring ensures unauthorized changes are detected quickly and provides audit trail for compliance.

input_fields.label: Number of managed systems
input_fields.helper: Nodes managed by Ansible, Puppet, Chef, etc.

name: Business Transaction Logs
description: Application-level business transaction logs including order processing, payment systems, and ERP activity.
whyItMatters: Business transaction logs enable detection of fraud, revenue leakage, and application abuse that security-only tools cannot identify.
